title.value: Connectivity alterations in autism reflect functional idiosyncrasy
title.justification: The title prominently reflects the core investigation of the paper, which is about exploring how connectivity alterations in autism are linked to functional idiosyncrasy.
title.quote: Connectivity alterations in autism reflect functional idiosyncrasy

analysis.description: The paper explores the relationship between connectivity alterations in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and functional idiosyncrasy through a novel approach. Using a multi-centric dataset, it profiles inter-individual variability in functional network organization, focusing on differences in connectivity between individuals with ASD and typically developing controls. The study finds increased idiosyncrasy in certain brain networks in ASD and suggests that this idiosyncrasy contributes to connectivity alterations and observed inconsistencies in the autism connectomics literature. This research provides new biomarkers for studying atypical brain development in autism.

type.justification: The study involves an empirical investigation utilizing neuroimaging data from real-world subjects to analyze functional network idiosyncrasy in autism spectrum disorder.
type.quote: Studying a multi-centric dataset with 157 ASD and 172 TD, we obtained robust evidence for increased idiosyncrasy in ASD relative to TD in default mode, somatomotor and attention networks, but also reduced idiosyncrasy in lateral temporal cortices.

name.justification: The research focuses on using neuroimaging techniques to explore brain connectivity and variability in autism spectrum disorder, making it a subfield of neuroimaging with a specific emphasis on ASD.
name.quote: Neuroimaging-based phenotyping of the autism spectrum.

name.justification: The study investigates functional connectivity alterations specifically in relation to autism spectrum disorder, which places it within the functional connectivity subfield.
name.quote: Numerous neuroimaging studies based on resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) have indicated that autistic individuals often present with a mosaic pattern of connectivity alterations between distributed cortical regions relative to typically developing (TD) controls.

name.value: Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE I and II)
name.justification: The ABIDE datasets are central to the study, providing the neuroimaging data necessary to explore connectivity patterns in ASD.
name.quote: We studied idiosyncrasy based on rs-fMRI data from both waves of the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE I and II).

referenced_paper_title.value: The autism brain imaging data exchange: towards a large-scale evaluation of the intrinsic brain architecture in autism
referenced_paper_title.justification: The ABIDE dataset is referenced as a critical dataset utilized in the study for analyzing brain connectivity in autism.
